- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.  
- When true price declines sharply after a peak, model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior 3–5 period average + 10–20% of recent drop.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model often overreacts to short-term noise; use 3-period moving average to smooth forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% to align with observed downward drift.  
- If sentiment history shows no recent positive signals, avoid aggressive upward forecasts; cap maximum price increase at 1.5x recent 7-day average.
